descriptors.definition: Entities must provide disclosures enabling users to evaluate the nature and financial effects of their business activities and economic environments. This disclosure mandates presenting operational insights from the exact perspective utilized by the entity's management.
inclusion: Financial effects of business activities
Economic environment factors impacting operations
exclusion: Segments reported in separate financial statements when consolidated statements exist
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general financial disclosures by enforcing a strict management viewpoint rather than standardized financial metric groupings.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies to companies required to follow Indian Accounting Standards notified under the Companies Act, 2013. When separate financial statements are presented alongside consolidated statements, segment information is required exclusively in the consolidated financial statements.
inclusion: Companies under notified Indian Accounting Standards
exclusion: Non-compliant disclosures labeled as segment information by exempt entities
Parent's separate financial statements when consolidated statements are present
nearby_distinctions: Restricts mandatory segment reporting exclusively to consolidated financial reports rather than duplicate separate filings.

descriptors.definition: An operating segment is an entity component engaging in business activities that earn revenues and incur expenses, whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, and for which discrete financial information is available. This approach relies entirely on the internal organizational structure utilized by management rather than generalized risk and return assessments.
inclusion: Start-up operations yet to earn revenues
Components with internal review by the CODM and discrete financial data
exclusion: Components lacking discrete financial information or regular review by the CODM
nearby_distinctions: Replaces the risk and return approach of AS 17 with the management approach focused on internal resource allocation.

descriptors.concept_name: Functions that are integral to business
descriptors.definition: Internal functional units integral to a company's operations, such as research and development, qualify as operating segments if discrete information exists and the chief operating decision maker regularly reviews their results. Similarly, discontinued operations meeting standard business activity, review, and discrete data criteria qualify as operating segments.
inclusion: Research and development functions with discrete reviewed data
Discontinued operations engaging in business activities with reviewed results
exclusion: Integral functions lacking discrete financial metrics or regular management review
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes internal support functions from ordinary revenue-generating segments by requiring active CODM review and discrete data.

descriptors.concept_name: Discontinued Operations – Whether An Operating Segment
descriptors.definition: Discontinued operations meet the definition of an operating segment if they continue engaging in business activities, their operating results are reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, and supporting discrete information is available. Merely examining revenue data alone without broader performance measures may fail to establish an operating segment unless aligned with specific market-building strategies.
inclusion: Discontinued units with ongoing business activities and discrete review data
exclusion: Units devoid of ongoing operational activity or management performance tracking
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates terminated business lines from active segments by requiring active persistence in business activities and active CODM oversight.

descriptors.definition: Entities must report separate information for each operating segment that is identified individually, results from aggregating multiple segments, or exceeds established quantitative thresholds. Additional specific situations defined by the standard may also mandate separate segment reporting.
inclusion: Segments exceeding quantitative thresholds
Aggregated segments meeting combination criteria
exclusion: Operating segments falling below thresholds and not meeting aggregation or utility criteria
nearby_distinctions: Separates broad operating segments from subsets that warrant individual reporting via quantitative metrics or aggregation rules.

descriptors.definition: Two or more operating segments can be combined into a single segment if they exhibit similar long-term financial performance and economic characteristics. Furthermore, the segments must align with the core principle and share identical traits regarding products, production processes, customer types, distribution methods, and regulatory environments.
inclusion: Segments sharing similar gross margins, products, processes, customers, and distribution methods
exclusion: Segments operating under distinct regulatory rules or conflicting economic environments without comparable metrics
nearby_distinctions: Permits consolidation of distinct operating units only when strict qualitative and economic likeness conditions are mutually met.

descriptors.definition: An operating segment becomes reportable if its reported revenue, absolute profit or loss, or assets equal or exceed 10% of the combined totals for all operating segments. Management may also discretionally report segments failing these numeric tests if deemed useful for financial statement users.
inclusion: Segments representing 10% or more of combined segment revenues
Segments holding 10% or more of absolute profit/loss or total assets
exclusion: Segments below the 10% limits unless voluntarily selected by management for user utility
nearby_distinctions: Applies strict mathematical cutoff values to isolate significant segments, distinct from discretionary management grouping.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose general information, performance measures, assets, liabilities, and measurement bases for each period presenting profit or loss statements. Comprehensive reconciliations linking segment totals back to corresponding entity-wide financial statement amounts must also be provided.
inclusion: General organizational factors and aggregation judgments
Reconciliations of segment revenues, assets, and liabilities to entity totals
exclusion: Unreconciled segment figures or missing prior period restatements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes core segment performance metrics from mandatory reconciliations required to tie internal reports to official financial statements.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose the factors utilized to identify reportable segments, encompassing organizational bases like products, services, or geography. Disclosures must also cover management judgments applied during segment aggregation and descriptions of products and services generating segment revenues.
inclusion: Organizational factors used for segment identification
Descriptions of products and services per reportable segment
exclusion: Omission of management judgment rationale or aggregation criteria descriptions
nearby_distinctions: Provides qualitative context regarding segment identification, supplementing the quantitative numerical tables.

descriptors.concept_name: Information about profit or loss, assets and liabilities
descriptors.definition: Entities must report measures of profit or loss, total assets, and total liabilities for each reportable segment if regularly provided to the chief operating decision maker. Specific supplementary financial items like interest, depreciation, and equity-accounted investments must also be disclosed when included in metrics reviewed by the CODM.
inclusion: Revenues from external customers and intersegment transactions
Additions to non-current assets excluding financial instruments and tax assets
exclusion: Items never reviewed by the CODM and excluded from internal reporting measures
nearby_distinctions: Ties mandatory reporting items directly to the internal data package reviewed by the CODM rather than imposing universal line-item checklists.

descriptors.definition: Reported segment items must align with the exact measures supplied to the chief operating decision maker for resource allocation and performance evaluation. Entities must provide clear explanations of measurement bases, transaction accounting between segments, and the nature of differences separating segment totals from entity-wide financial figures.
inclusion: Measures matching internal CODM reporting standards
Explanations of measurement differences between segments and entity financials
exclusion: Arbitrary cost allocations lacking a reasonable basis
nearby_distinctions: Mandates that segment accounting rules mirror internal management reporting tools rather than standardizing separate independent measurement policies.
